top5.title: U.S. blocks the overseas rental of Chinese AI chips
top5.description: The Trump administration is implementing new export controls to prevent Chinese companies from remotely accessing AI chips and data centers located in other countries. The rule will require licenses for infrastructure capable of providing more than 12 million TPP.
top5.why: The U.S. is tightening controls to prevent Chinese companies from remotely accessing advanced AI chips and overseas data centers, with major implications for global infrastructure and technology supply chains.

top5.title: Anthropic’s IPO becomes a test for the entire AI sector
top5.description: The creator of Claude is set to list on the Nasdaq at between 70 and 78 dollars per share, amid a difficult environment for AI and Nvidia. Anthropic plans to spend more than 900 billion dollars with suppliers despite a 104-billion-dollar loss over nine months.
top5.why: Anthropic’s planned IPO will be a crucial test of investor appetite for AI companies and could reset expectations for the sector’s enormous spending and losses.

top5.title: SpaceX completes first catch of a Starship returning from orbit
top5.description: On Saturday, SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft with the mechanical arms of its launch tower in Texas. The spacecraft released 26 Starlink satellites and completed 14 trips around Earth, but the Super Heavy booster exploded during its descent.
top5.why: SpaceX’s first successful orbital Starship catch demonstrates meaningful progress toward a reusable heavy-lift system that could transform launch economics, despite the booster failure.

top5.title: A compromised MCP server can hijack an AI agent’s other tools
top5.description: A test cited by VentureBeat found that a compromised MCP server could prompt an agent connected to five servers to misuse the other tools in 78.3% of cases. The article recommends limiting credentials, adding human approvals, and logging the entire call chain.
top5.why: The finding that a compromised MCP server can hijack an AI agent’s other tools in most tested cases exposes a major security risk as companies deploy interconnected agents.

top5.title: Nvidia, AMD, Google, and Meta join open inference consortium
top5.description: LMSYS launched the SGLang Consortium to coordinate engineering work on its open-source AI inference engine, with Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Google, and Meta among its founding members. Members will contribute deployment feedback, testing, and development, while SGLang maintainers will retain control over technical decisions.
top5.why: The SGLang Consortium brings Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Google and Meta together around open-source inference infrastructure, potentially influencing the cost and portability of large-scale AI deployment.
